title: Want More Godzilla? Check Out Netflix’s Anime Movie Trilogy
content:
After the release of Godzilla Minus Zero , the smash-hit follow-up to 2023’s Godzilla Minus One , fans of the kaiju franchise have been clamoring to find more content featuring their favorite reptilian titan. Thankfully, the Godzilla franchise has 72-years worth of content for fans to dive into, including Netflix’s three part film series from Toho Animation and Polygon Pictures. Consisting of Godzilla: Planet of the Monsters , Godzilla: City on the Edge of Battle and Godzilla: The Planet Eater , this action-packed sci-fi trilogy tells a high-stakes story.

Initially introduced as a revenge journey that later pivots to focusing on the struggle between humans and nature, hubris, and the philosophy of what gives us an indomitable drive to survive, this unique Godzilla trilogy was penned by none other than Gen Urobuchi, a prolific and infamous writer known for his work on franchises like Puella Magi Madoka Magica , Psycho-Pass , and even legendary tokusatsu such as Kamen Rider Gaim . True to his other works, all three of these Godzilla films take their time unraveling their overarching narrative, using the legendary figure of Godzilla to aid in exploring the psychology of each of the main characters .

The Netflix Godzilla Trilogy Reinvents The Legendary Kaiju In a Fascinating Way

Opening with Godzilla: Planet of the Monsters in 2017 , the trilogy begins by introducing audiences to a group of human refugees returning to the planet Earth to attempt to recolonize it 20,000 years after being chased away by the titular kaiju. The film also introduces two alien species that worked in tandem when Earth was lost to the beast, known as the Exif, a group of religious zealots, as well as the technologically advanced Bilusaludo. After their failure to aid humanity in defeating Godzilla, humans emigrated to an exoplanet called “Tau-e.”

The film’s protagonist, Haruo Sakaki, holds a bitter hatred toward the kaiju and has made a vow to destroy it and reclaim Earth for humanity after deciding that Tau-e is inhabitable for human-kind’s continued existence. The first film follows many story beats akin to a typical revenge story, but as the plot unravels it becomes clear that the first film is aiming to set up a “humans versus nature” conflict. Without giving too many details away, Planet of the Monsters leaves off on a cliffhanger that leads perfectly into its 2018 follow-up film, Godzilla: City on the Edge of Battle .

Godzilla: City on the Edge of Battle introduces another fan-favorite kaiju : Mechagodzilla who aids the returning human cast in their efforts to defeat Godzilla. The film is a direct sequel, opening shortly after the first entry’s cliffhanger ending. The third and final film in the trilogy, The Planet Eater , leans heavily into themes of existential dread and human psychology, with the same extraterrestrial forces who once vowed to help humanity in their efforts now outwardly acting with hostility toward them due to differences in priorities when handling the threat of the giant kaiju threatening their recolonization efforts.

This film explores many classic story beats embedded into the roots of the Godzilla franchise as well, drawing comparisons between the beast and human-made tragedies. Directed in a collaborative effort by Kobun Shizuno ( Detective Conan, Evangelion: 1.0 You Are (Not) Alone ) and Hiroyuki Seshita ( Knights of Sidonia, Ajin ), the trilogy is uniquely positioned in how it presents these story beats, as it’s the first Godzilla trilogy to commit fully to some of the franchise’s sci-fi leanings and even giving Godzilla mutations akin to films like Shin Godzilla .

Godzilla ‘s Anime Trilogy’s Production Staff Knew Exactly What They Were Doing With The Iconic Monster

While the overall reception to the Netflix Godzilla trilogy is mixed in regards to how well the films stand as proper entries to the franchise, it’s clear to see what the filmmaking team wanted to do with the story. In that, all three films beautifully accomplish exactly what they set out to do. Gen Urobuchi’s scriptwriting prowess really hits its stride in the second film as the main cast’s goals begin to unravel as they reckon with the consequences of pitting advanced technology against a hulking beast that’s inhabited the Earth for well over 20,000 years.

Additionally, it’s easy to see just how well the directing duo Kobun Shizuno and Hiroyuki Seshita understand psychological storytelling as it pertains to science fiction as a genre. The pair are able to showcase stunning sci-fi action sequences and large-scale kaiju fights that are interspersed with deeply compelling conversations about humanities position on the intergalactic food chain.All of this is only amplified by the absolutely phenomenal vocal performances found throughout the film trilogy, including Mamoru Miyano’s role as the protagonist, Haruo Sakaki.

Mamoru Miyano has without a doubt positioned himself as an A-list casting choice for any anime series or film out there, with casting credits including legendary characters like Doma in Demon Slayer , Chrollo in Hunter x Hunter , and Light Yagami in Death Note . Other performances throughout the trilogy include other huge names in the industry, Takahiro Sakurai, Kana Hanazawa, Yuki Kaji, and Daisuke Ono.

For any Godzilla fan looking for a narratively compelling, bittersweet story of humanities conflict with nature, especially after the heartbreaking conclusion of Godzilla Minus Zero , there’s truly no better option than binging Netflix’s Godzilla trilogy. Have you checked out this trilogy yet? If so, what do you think of this take on Godzilla? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

title: 'Giant Ojousama' Reveals Additional Cast, Character Promo
content:
The official X (formerly Twitter) account for the television anime adaptation of Q Nikumura 's Giant Ojousama manga revealed additional cast and three character promotional videos on Friday. The anime is scheduled to premiere in January 2027.

Cast Madoka Itou: Risa Imayanagi ( Nokemono-tachi no Yoru ) Stella: Rina Kawaguchi ( Needy Girl Overdose ) Gimlet: Ryoutarou Okiayu ( Kanan-sama wa Akumade Choroi )

Hiroshi Ikehata ( Witch Watch ) is directing at Tatsunoko Production . Yuu Satou ( Haite Kudasai, Takamine-san ) is handling the series composition and penning the script. Hajime Mitsuda ( Akiba's Trip The Animation ) is designing the characters.

Yuusuke Shirato (Dream Monster) ( Kunoichi Tsubaki no Mune no Uchi ), Kijibato (Dream Monster) ( Ijiranaide, Nagatoro-san 2nd Attack ending theme song composition), and Aira (Dream Monster) ( Kaya-chan wa Kowakunai opening theme song composition) are composing the music.

Nikumura originally posted the manga on Shounen Jump+ web magazine's Jump Rookie! section as an entry for the monthly award in December 2020. Following a readers vote, it won the Bronze Rookie Award for December. A total of four chapters were released by February 2021.

Sunday Webry began serializing the action comedy manga in July 2021. Shogakukan published the 13th volume on September 11, with the 14th volume scheduled to be released on December 11.

title: The Dragon Prince's Ill-Mated Betrothal Manga Ends, Gets 3-Chapter Epilogue
content:
Manga artist Sango Sansan 's manga adaptation of Nanaki Ichinose 's The Dragon Prince's Ill-Mated Betrothal light novel series ended with its 32nd chapter, which NTT Solmare 's Comic CMOA manga service published on September 17. With the manga's ending, Sansan also announced that author Ichinose has penned a manga-original epilogue story, which are being published in three chapters. Comic CMOA published epilogue chapter 33 on October 17 and chapter 34 on November 17.

Yen Press licensed the manga and will publish the first volume on January 26. The company describes the story:

Adeline, daughter of an earl, receives an offer of engagement from the Dragonkin Realm on her seventeenth birthday. All Dragonkins must find their "Mate," and they want her for their third prince. Soon, amid scorn and criticism, she realizes she's an unwilling participant in a twisted—and deadly—plot. But the story doesn't end there! 250 years later, history begins to repeat itself with another invitation...and the unknown secrets that lie beyond it.

Sansan launched the manga adaptation on Comic CMOA in July 2024. Kadokawa published the manga's fifth compiled book volume on November 17.

Ichinose launched the original story on the Shōsetsuka ni Narō website in 2018. Kadokawa published the first novel volume with original character design by Noco Sugimachi in March 2024. The fourth volume shipped on November 25.

title: MangaPlaza Add Seven Seas Titles to Catalogue
content:
Some of the titles coming to the platform include:

• Mushoku Tensei - Jobless Reincarnation - Rifujin na Magonote, Yuka Fujikawa

• Though I Am an Inept Villainess: Tale of the Butterfly-Rat Body Swap in the Maiden Court - Satsuki Nakamura, Ei Ohitsuji

• The Exiled Heavy Knight Knows How to Game the System (Omnibus) - Nekoko, Brocco Lee, Jaian

• The Saint’s Magic Power is Omnipotent - Yuka Tachibana, Fujiazuki

• The Strange House - Uketsu, Kyō Ayano

The platform will also run a point reward promotion for all Seven Seas titles.

NTT Solmare Corp launched MangaPlaza , a digital contents library for manga and Japanese publications in the United States, in spring 2022. MangaPlaza offers original titles that have yet to get English releases, along with titles from other publishers such as Kodansha .

NTT Solmare is a subsidiary of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone West Corporation.

title: Sword Art Online Creator’s New Anime Has a Chance to Be the Next Big Hit
content:
Earlier this month, an action fantasy anime by the creator of Sword Art Online made its debut, and it’s already one of the most unique series in recent years. Sword Art Online is one of those 2010s classics that are still relevant to this day. Not only is the world-building incredible, but the exceptional storytelling, complex characters, and the exciting plot twists keep fans hooked to the show until the very end. The novel’s author, Reki Kawahara, doesn’t shy away from showing the brutality of the world where the story is set, just so fans are aware of the high stakes.

Throughout his career, Kawahara has worked on a few stories, and each of them stands out in one way or the other. This also includes Devil’s Crest that made its debut on Prime Video on November 6th. While the anime had a late start compared to the other Fall 2026 shows, it’s easily one of the best anime of the year. The anime is based on an ongoing novel written by Kawahara. While it’s too soon to determine if the anime is already a major hit, it has the potential to be one of the biggest hits in recent years. Luckily, the premiere generated enough hype, especially considering fans of Sword Art Online would be interested in another show by the same creator.

Devil’s Crest Deserves to Be a Bigger Hit Than Sword Art Online

The story is still in its initial phase as it introduces fans to the main characters, the unique premise, and the expansive world-building. What truly sets this anime apart is that it offers a completely new outlook on stories centering around a virtual reality game. In Sword Art Online , the characters in the first major arc were physically trapped inside a virtual reality MMORPG and could not log out. This premise isn’t only limited to Sword Art Online , but many such anime focus on the characters entering the game world as they try to survive while also trying to figure out a way to return home.

However, Devils’ Crest switches things up by bringing the virtual reality into the real world. The story focuses on a group of middle school students who never could’ve imagined that playing a new virtual reality game would not only turn their world upside down, but also plunge their world into chaos. Instead of being trapped inside the video game world, they realize that the game world blends into the real world, raising the stakes much higher than any other isekai show.

Another thing that sets Devils’ Crest apart is that it has a much darker tone, as the first couple of episodes portray an unimaginable level of brutality and gruesome moments. This is something even Sword Art Online didn’t feature , even though it has intense moments throughout the story. The anime has released four episodes as of now, and it’s safe to say that the story is finally taking shape as the central group is now learning how to defeat the monsters and save their world.

How are you liking Devils’ Crest so far, and would you be keeping up with the weekly episodes? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Killer Shark in Another World Anime Adaptation Announced
content:
An anime adaptation of Killer Shark in Another World manga by Kuboken has been announced. A teaser visual and trailer were also released. Studio Lings is animating the series.

Shige Fukase is directing the anime adaptation with Shigeru Murakoshi in charge of the series composition. Nozomi Ikuyama is on character designs, while Iroha Mitsuki is on shark design, and Keiji Inai is composing the music.

Kill Time Communication’s Comic Valkyrie magazine is serializing the manga since 2020. Seven Seas Entertainment is publishing the title in English, describing it as: Everyone thought Shiromi Lovecut-Toothrough was the worst summoner in the world. But after she summons Sharkiller, a creature capable of transforming into Hollywood’s most ferocious B-movie sharks, nobody’s laughing now! In fact, they’re running for their lives! With her bloodthirsty buddy chomping at the bit to kill everyone in sight, can Shiromi defeat the Demon King and end his reign of terror? Or maybe the realm would be better off if she didn’t…? Source: Killer Shark in Another World anime Official X (formerly Twitter) , website © 2021 Kuboken / KILL TIME COMMUNICATION / Isekai Kuimetsu no Same Production Committee

title: Manga 'Isekai Kuimetsu no Same' Receives TV Anime Adaptation
content:
An official website opened for a television anime adaptation of Kuboken 's Isekai Kuimetsu no Same ( Killer Shark in Another World ) on Thursday, revealing staff, a teaser visual (pictured), and a teaser promotional video.

Staff Director: Shigeru Fukase ( Shin Shinka no Mi: Shiranai Uchi ni Kachigumi Jinsei ) Series Composition, Script: Shigeru Murakoshi ( Ballpark de Tsukamaete! ) Character Design: Sou Ikuyama ( Watashi wo Tabetai, Hitodenashi ) Shark Design: Iroha Mitsuki ( Shin Shinka no Mi: Shiranai Uchi ni Kachigumi Jinsei character design) Music: Keiji Inai ( Dungeon ni Deai wo Motomeru no wa Machigatteiru Darou ka ) Production: Infinite Studio: Studio Lings

Kuboken began serializing the fantasy comedy manga in Comic Valkyrie in October 2020. Kill Time Communication published the 12th volume on July 8.

Seven Seas Entertainment licensed the series in English in February 2024. The seventh volume was released on July 7, with the eighth volume scheduled for a January 2027 release.

But after she summons Sharkiller, a creature capable of transforming into Hollywood's most ferocious B-movie sharks, nobody's laughing now! In fact, they're running for their lives! With her bloodthirsty buddy chomping at the bit to kill everyone in sight, can Shiromi defeat the Demon King and end his reign of terror? Or maybe the realm would be better off if she didn't...?

title: Netflix’s Solo Leveling Hit With a Major Production Shake-Up Barely Two Episodes In
content:
Netflix’s Solo Leveling live-action faces a major staff change just two episodes into filming, potentially affecting the rest of the production. When the project was first announced, it was revealed that Lee Haejun and Kim Byung-seo would co-direct the series. The duo already had an established working relationship, having previously collaborated on the 2019 action-adventure film Ashfall . The staff looked promising, and recent updates suggested that production had been progressing smoothly. However, a recent report from South Korean publication OSEN has revealed the production’s first major shake-up. Director Lee Haejun has stepped down from the series after just two episodes of filming were completed.

According to the report, Han Dongwook will replace him and work alongside Kim Byung-seo as co-director for the remainder of the series. OSEN also reported that the decision involved the production committee , Netflix, and Lee Haejun, with all parties mutually agreeing to his departure. The change was reportedly made amicably rather than due to any conflict or differences in interest. While it is a good sign that production is continuing, fans may still feel disappointed, especially given the established working dynamic between Lee Haejun and Kim Byung-seo.

Netflix’s Solo Leveling Director Lee Haejun Steps Down After Just Two Episodes of Filming

While it is concerning that the series’ lead director has stepped down midway through production, another update from a South Korean publication suggests that these changes may have been planned rather than sudden. According to Newsen , which received an update from the production team itself, the series is one of the projects where different directors handle individual episodes. Lee Haejun directed the first two episodes, while the remaining episodes will be handled by Kim Byung-seo and Han Dongwook. While the accuracy of this explanation remains unclear, it is good news that filming for the project is still progressing.

The main point for fans to focus on is whether Han Dongwook will be a suitable replacement for Lee Haejun. His track record suggests that he could be a good choice. Although Dongwook has not previously worked as a lead director, he has considerable experience with series that feature crime thrillers and romance. This bodes well for Solo Leveling , especially since the series appears to be taking the latter element more seriously. title: kuboken's Killer Shark in Another World Manga Gets TV Anime
content:
Kadokawa announced on Friday kuboken 's Killer Shark in Another World ( Isekai Kuimetsu no Same ) manga will get a television anime adaptation.

Shige Fukase ( Hamidashi Creative ; episode director for That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime , Vinland Saga ) is directing the anime at Studio Lings . Shigeru Murakoshi ( Snowball Earth , Dark Gathering , I Parry Everything ) is both writing and overseeing the series scripts. Nozomi Ikuyama ( This Monster Wants to Eat Me , The Final-Boss Prince is Somehow Obsessed with the Chubby Villainess ) is designing the characters. Iroha Mizuki is in charge of shark design, and Keiji Inai ( Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon? franchise) is composing the music. Infinite is producing the series.

Everyone thought Shiromi Lovecut-Toothrough was the worst summoner in the world. But after she summons Sharkiller, a creature capable of transforming into Hollywood's most ferocious B-movie sharks, nobody's laughing now! In fact, they're running for their lives! With her bloodthirsty buddy chomping at the bit to kill everyone in sight, can Shiromi defeat the Demon King and end his reign of terror? Or maybe the realm would be better off if she didn't...?

kuboken launched the manga in Kill Time Communication 's Comic Valkyrie magazine in October 2020. Kill Time Communication published the 12th compiled volume on July 8.

title: Fool Night Anime Reveals 3 More Cast Members
content:
The official website for the television anime of Kasumi Yasuda 's Fool Night manga revealed three more cast members on Thursday.

Previously announced cast members include:

• Kōki Uchiyama as Toshiro Kamiya

• Minako Kotobuki as Yomiko Horai

• Junya Enoki as Akira Yatsuka

• Aya Endō as Saeko Kanaeno

• Kiyomitsu Mizuuchi as Jin Hiragishi

• Shion Wakayama as Sumi Matsuno

• The late Hiroshi Tsuchida as Ken Hikasa

• Nobuhiko Okamoto as Nishi

• Sayaka Senbongi as Meg Okumura

• Yumiko Kobayashi as Ivy

Atsuyuki Yukawa ( Suzume unit director) directed the anime at Sunrise and SHAFT . Jin Tanaka ( Oshi no Ko ) wrote the scripts. Robert Satō designed the characters. Tatsuya Katō ( Dr. Stone ) composed the music.

Other staff members include:

• Assistant Director: Ryō Shimura

• Visual Development: Ryō Kikuchi

• Art Director: Maki Takano (J.C. Staff)

• Color Design: Jin Hibino

• Director of Photography: Mana Ishikawa (animocaramel), Chiaki Tokuda (Tera Effect), Takayuki Aizu (SHAFT)

• CG Directors: Naoki Yamamoto, Junya Hirano

• Editing: Rie Matsubara (Seyama Editing Room)

• Sound Director: Yōta Tsuruoka

The band Tempalay performs the opening theme song "Shake! spit out," and Nowlu performs the ending theme song "Iki" (Breath).

Viz Media licensed the manga, and it describes the story:

Kamiya is at the end of his rope. His mother is ill, and his job barely pays for her medication, much less food. With few options left, he considers the life-changing process of transfloration. Ready to give his body up for a payday, Kamiya is about to explore the limits of society's waning humanity.

Yasuda launched the manga in Shogakukan 's Big Comic Superior magazine in November 2020. Shogakukan will ship the manga's 14th compiled book volume on November 30. The manga has crossed one million copies in circulation worldwide as of this month.

The manga ranked #12 in the male reader list of the 2023 edition of Takarajimasha 's Kono Manga ga Sugoi! (This Manga Is Amazing!) guidebook.
